policy.normal_basis: For the counter increment property, this independently pinned head has the same +2/+1 operations and both participate in the same initialized mutex. Its first-group analysis is complete for this property and produced zero candidates.

common_protection.explanation: Both worker bodies directly update the single file-scope ordinary int counter. writer_a holds mutex across its update. writer_b executes its entire update without synchronization. main creates both workers before joining either, permitting overlapping worker execution. The subsequent joins order worker completion before the final main-thread read. They supply no happens-before ordering between the two worker updates.

patch.reason: This bounded review is read-only. Patch generation belongs to the host-controlled patch stage.

review.recommended_action: Restore acquisition and release of the existing mutex around writer_b's complete counter++ operation so both worker updates follow the same exclusive-lock protocol.
review.summary: The PR removes writer_b's mutex acquisition and release around counter++ at workers.c line 14. writer_a concurrently performs counter += 2 at workers.c line 8. Both accesses resolve directly to the same ordinary int declared at workers.c line 3. The supplied complete worker bodies and thread-creation sequence establish conflicting updates without common synchronization, introducing a C data race and undefined behavior. The diff and impact scope directly connect the removed locking to this access pair. Status respects the supplied coverage.candidate_decision.max_status value of probable.
verification_recommendations: Have the host verify that both worker updates hold the same mutex throughout each read-modify-write operation.
Under the host-approved verification plan, exercise successful creation and completion of both workers with overlapping execution and check that the final counter is 3 and observe returns 4.
